quarterly_data.signal: Relay's Q2 2026 results release (clinical highlights): the zovegalisib plus atirmociclib triplet showed a 44% objective response rate in heavily pre-treated CDK4/6-experienced patients (median 3L) with PI3Kα-mutated, HR+/HER2- metastatic breast cancer at unoptimized doses, with ORR similar across kinase and non-kinase PIK3CA mutations and adverse events consistent with those previously reported by each molecule. Initial Phase 1/2 ReInspire data in vascular anomalies were presented at the ISSVA World Congress 2026: in the Part 1 dose randomization portion for adults and adolescents ages 12 and up, 60% of patients achieved a volumetric response at the earliest time point (12 weeks), and nearly all patients experienced symptomatic improvement at 12 weeks while maintaining a safety and tolerability profile showing the potential for chronic use; Relay opened expansion cohorts for adults and adolescents and continued dose escalation for pediatric patients age 6-11. The Phase 1/2 trial of the NRAS-selective inhibitor RLY-8161 continues in NRAS-mutant melanoma and other NRAS-mutant solid tumors. Anticipated milestones include an enrollment update for the Phase 3 ReDiscover-2 trial in 2L breast cancer by year-end 2026 and a vascular anomalies data and regulatory update by year-end 2026. Relay states zovegalisib has the potential, if approved, to address a significant portion of the approximately 140,000 patients with PI3Kα-mutated HR+/HER2- breast cancer and the estimated 170,000 patients with PI3Kα-driven vascular anomalies per year in the United States.
quarterly_data.figure: 44% ORR (median 3L, unoptimized doses); 60% volumetric response at 12 weeks (ages 12 and up); approximately 140,000 breast cancer and 170,000 vascular anomalies patients per year (U.S.)
